day: # The readings of Lutheran Service Book (2006), kept by the LCMS and
# Lutheran Church-Canada (each names it with `readings,lsb`; the rows are
# keyed by the day ids their days.csv share): the three-year series (rows
# with variant three-year and cycle A, B or C), the one-year series (variant
# one-year), the feasts and festivals (both), and the Daily Lectionary (both).
# The sources of each part are named above it.
# Lutheran Service Book (Concordia Publishing House / LCMS, 2006), THREE-YEAR lectionary (Series A, B, C)
# Sundays and principal festivals, plus LSB's fixed-date Feasts and Festivals, Reformation and All Saints (variant and cycle blank).
# Cycle A = church year beginning Advent 2025, 2028 ... (LSB "Series A").
# Checked against the LCMS Commission on Worship's Church Year Calendars with the readings of 2024-25 (Series C), 2025-26 (A) and 2026-27 (B),
#   copies supplied by the maintainer, November 2026): every Sunday and festival those years have agrees, psalms included, but for the two
#   psalms taken from them (C Easter Day Psalm 16, where YAAG has the Sunrise psalm 118:15-29; C Proper 9 Psalm 66:1-7) and the readings
#   where they differ from LSB itself, which is followed (docs/source-errors.csv). Not in those years: A Epiphany 6-8 and Propers 3-4,
#   B Epiphany 5-8 and Proper 3, C Epiphany 8 and Propers 3-6.
#   The LCMS Lectionary Summaries (Series A 2025-26, B, C, Feasts and Festivals; files.lcms.org/d/lectionary-summaries, without psalms) agree as well.
# Primary source (OT, Psalm, Epistle, Gospel): Year At A Glance, "Church Year LSB Series A/B/C" tables, https://yaag.org/lang.php?myYear=YYYY&myLang=en&series=3
# Cross-checks: Wartburg Project, LSB 3-Year A/B/C and Feasts, Festivals, and Occasions pages (OT/Epistle/Gospel only, no psalms)
#   LutheranLectionary.org 3-Year Series A table (with psalms), https://lutheranlectionary.org/ (Series A, Advent 1 to Proper 21, fully agrees);
#   Concordia Publishing House blog feast-day reading posts, https://blog.cph.org/read/topic/feast (feast psalms);
#   St. John's Lutheran (Fort Collins) wiki, https://www.stjohnsfc.org/wiki/index.php/Year_B (psalms of B Epiphany 7/8, B/C Proper 3, C Epiphany 8, St. Michael).
# Psalm antiphon verses printed by YAAG (e.g. "Psalm 122 (6)") are dropped; parenthesized verse RANGES are kept as optional verses.
# Propers 3-28 are keyed by LSB date ranges (Proper 3 = Sunday May 24-28 ... Proper 28 = Nov 13-19); Proper 29 = last_sunday.
#   B Epiphany 7 & 8, C Epiphany 8: OT/Epistle/Gospel from Wartburg only; psalms (41; 103:1-13; 92) from St. John's wiki only.
#   B & C Proper 3: OT/Epistle/Gospel from Wartburg + St. John's wiki (both give Epistle Acts 2:14a, 36-47); psalms (103:1-13; 112:1-9) wiki only.
#   Easter Sunrise (title "Easter Sunrise"): Wartburg, checked against LSB; psalm for A from LutheranLectionary.org, for B and C (Psalm 118:15-29) from the LCMS Church Year Calendars.
#   C Maundy Thursday "or Exodus 12 / 1 Cor 11 / John 13" alternatives: Wartburg only (YAAG lists only Jeremiah 31 / Hebrews 10 / Luke 22).
#   Psalms of Series B and C rest on YAAG and the LCMS calendars above (the days those calendars lack, on YAAG alone).
#   Christmas Dawn psalm: YAAG 2019, 2020 and LutheranLectionary.org give Psalm 98; YAAG 2021 gives Psalm 97.

# Discrepancies (YAAG followed unless noted; every one below checked against LSB itself, pp. xiv-xxiii, October 2026): B Proper 15 epistle Eph 5:6-21 (Wartburg 5:6-20); B Proper 23 gospel Mark 10:17-22 (Wartburg 10:17-27);
#   C Epiphany 4 gospel Luke 4:31-44 (Wartburg 4:31-40); C Lent 5 gospel Luke 20:9-20 (Wartburg 20:9-19); C Easter 5 epistle Rev 21:1-7 (Wartburg 21:1-6);

#   C Proper 14 gospel Luke 12:22-34 (35-40) as LSB prints it (YAAG omits the optional verses; Wartburg "12:22-34, 35-40"); C Advent 4 gospel (46-56) and C Proper 16 Hebrews 12:4-24 (25-29) follow Wartburg (YAAG typos);
#   C Easter 2 OT Acts 5:12-20 (21-32) (Wartburg typo "15:12"); St. Peter & St. Paul OT Acts 15:1-12 (13-21) (Wartburg; CPH blog "15:1-21");
#   Presentation gospel Luke 2:22-32 (33-40) and New Year's Eve OT Isaiah 30:(8-14) 15-17 follow Wartburg/LutheranLectionary.org (CPH blog prints without parentheses).
# Feast psalms of St. Thomas, St. Joseph, the Annunciation, St. Philip & St. James, the 31 May Visitation, the Nativity of St. John
#   the Baptist, St. Mary Magdalene and St. James of Jerusalem: from the Altar Book (Propers of the Day, Feasts, Festivals, and
#   Occasions, pp. 943-985, photographed by the maintainer, October 2026), which agrees with every other feast's readings here.
#   St. Luke (147:1-11) and the 2 July Visitation (138) are from the LCMS Church Year Calendars (lcms.org PDFs, 2015-16 to 2026-27)
#   which list a feast when it falls on a Sunday. Feast OT/Epistle/Gospel: Wartburg, checked against CPH blog where available.

# Holy Saturday, Holy Week, Easter Monday-Wednesday and Pentecost Eve-Tuesday: from LSB itself (below the three-year propers); the Vigil's Service of Readings and the psalms of Holy Week and Easter week from the Altar Book (Series B and C, pp. 682-697 and 776-791). Reformation/All Saints: rows for the observed-Sunday ids and for 10-31 / 11-01 on weekdays.
# Extra kind: "procession" = Palm Sunday procession Gospel (John 12:12-19, all years).

day: # Lutheran Service Book (2006, LCMS), Daily Lectionary, LSB pp. 299-304 (also basis of Treasury of Daily Prayer).
# Source 1 (final text): "Daily Lectionary Reading Plan", taken from Lutheran Service Book pp. 299-304, (c) 2006 Concordia Publishing House
#   https://communication.cph.org/hubfs/_cph/2018/12/lutheran-life/daily-lectionary.pdf  -- used for Lent/Easter block, 1 Jan-9 Mar, 18 May-31 Aug, 27 Nov-31 Dec.
#   That copy lacks LSB p. 302 (1 Sep-26 Nov); that page was checked against a scan of the printed
#   LSB p. 302 (also at https://hymnary.org/hymn/LSB2006/page/222), with which the draft agrees, and its
#   optional (italic) readings were added from it.
# Source 2 (cross-check, and sole source for 1 Sep-26 Nov): "Daily Lectionary. From rough draft of Lutheran Service Book (to be published 2006)"
#   Its OT/NT columns match the final text almost everywhere (differences found: 9 Jan Ezek 3:12-28, 13 Dec Rev 1:1-19, 31 Jan 2 Tim 3:1-18, 21 Feb Job 16:1-21; final used).
#   Spot-checked 1 Sep-26 Nov against wartburgproject.org/daily (15 Sep, 21 Sep, 10 Oct, 30 Oct, 3 Nov, 16 Nov, 21 Nov agree; 5 Sep Wartburg has 2 Kings 4:1-17 vs draft 4:1-7).
# Keying: "The lectionary begins with Ash Wednesday. During the seasons of Lent and Easter ... the Church Year calendar is followed.
#   Following Holy Trinity Sunday, the calendar year is followed." So: Ash Wednesday (easter-46) through Holy Trinity (easter+56) use the movable
#   block keyed easter-46 ... easter+56 (Ascension = easter+39, Pentecost = easter+49). Dated rows 01-01..03-09 apply only when date lt easter-46;
#   dated rows 05-18..11-26 apply only when date gt easter+56; 11-27..12-31 apply every year. (Latest Ash Wed = 10 Mar, earliest Trinity = 17 May, so no gaps.)
# Kinds: ot, nt = the two assigned readings.  The sets titled "Daily Lectionary: Additional Reading" (ot, nt) are LSB's optional additional reading (printed in italics in LSB, for reading
#   more of the Bible); first identified as the citations in the final text that are absent from the draft's main columns, then checked
#   against the printed Pew Edition (pp. 299-304, a scan; October 2026): every one is in italics there, and no other reading is (the psalms
#   of Holy Week aside).  On 24 December both "Dan. 10:1-12:13" and "Is. 48:1-22" are in italics.
# psalm = the psalm printed in the reading rows (Palm Sunday 118, Holy Thursday 31, Good Friday 22).
# The psalms of LSB's table (p. 304, "The following seasonal psalm cycle may be used with the assigned readings in the Daily Lectionary")
#   are their own set, Psalms for Daily Prayer (psalm_morning, psalm_evening; the Psalm table box): the dated Christmas block
#   (24 Dec-6 Jan; the split of evening pairs, e.g. "132; 114", follows the text copy), and, at the end of this file, the weekday
#   tables for Advent (to 23 Dec), Lent (Ash Wednesday to Holy Saturday), Easter (to the Saturday after Pentecost) and the
#   four General weeks, which LSB gives to the season of Epiphany (from 7 Jan) and the Time of the Church (from Holy Trinity).
#   LSB says only that the General weeks "may be repeated as often as necessary"; here each of the two runs begins at Week 1
#   and goes on in turn, Week 1 to 4 and round again (inferred): in Epiphany the week 7 January falls in is Week 1, and after
#   Pentecost Holy Trinity begins Week 1.  The pre-Lent Sundays of the one-year series keep General.
#   Not included: LSB's note that Psalms 145-150 may also be prayed each morning (Sun 150, Mon 145, Tue 146, Wed 147:1-11,
#   Thu 147:12-20, Fri 148, Sat 149).  The table was read from the CPH copy (above); its Christmas block agrees with the text copy.
# Verse ranges normalized to en dash (LSB prints cross-chapter ranges with em dash); book names spelled out.
# Daily Lectionary: Additional Reading, continued: the draft's own additional readings (Source 2 above, LSB-Daily-Lectionary.pdf:
#   "with Additional Readings from the Apocrypha, the Lutheran Confessions, and the Catalog of Testimonies"), on the days LSB
#   gives none: kind apocrypha (in the KJV and RSV's chapters and verses, as the draft says) and confessions (the Book of
#   Concord, by part/article:paragraph as the draft cites it, Kolb-Wengert's paragraph numbers; the Apology's IV runs 1-400
#   and XII 1-178).  Abbreviations spelled out (SA, Tr., AC, Ap., FC SD, Cat. Test.); "Triglotta, pp. 11-27" is the

#   Preface to the Book of Concord in Triglot Concordia; "Apocr. parts of Esther" the Additions to Esther (Greek Esther, as Bible Gateway names it); Baruch 6 the Letter of Jeremiah (so named in the RSV); "Song of the 3
#   Child." the Song of the Three Young Men (with the Prayer of Azariah, KJV/RSV verses 1-68); "Prayer of Mannasseh"
#   corrected.  The draft gives its Bible additional readings a day earlier than LSB on 12-13 September (Hosea, Jonah)
#   and the Prayer of Manasseh on 14 September, beside 2 Chronicles 33; LSB's dates are kept and the prayer added
